historic_survey.survey: Mission Dolores Neighborhood Historic Context Statement, adopted 2022
historic_survey.finding: Recommended for further evaluation as a potential city landmark
historic_survey.note: Appears eligible for local designation under Criterion 3 (Architecture) as a rare remaining example of Gothic Revival institutional architecture in San Francisco. Character-defining features are the steeply pitched front gable roof, the fish-scale shingles, stucco cladding scored to resemble ashlar masonry, stained-glass lancet windows and a heavy wood panelled door. Drawn from a Planning Department DPR Primary Record of 2007.

historical_record.description: St. Nicholas Cathedral, affiliated with the Moscow Patriarchate, has occupied this address since leaving Divisadero Street.
The congregation renamed itself Bethel Evangelical Church.
The Russian Orthodox Church acquired the property and renamed it St. Nicholas Cathedral, adding the onion-domed finial and the Orthodox cross.
